# Curb

> An AI accessibility auditor that detects WCAG violations deterministically (axe-core via Playwright) and proposes code-level fixes that are verified by re-running axe against the patched DOM — the model never grades its own work. Built by Hiten Patel (https://hiten.dev).

Important framing: "verified" means an axe-core re-scan confirms the specific violation is resolved without introducing new ones. It does not replace expert human review — many WCAG criteria (alt-text adequacy, context, intent) require human judgement. Curb is a tool for developers and accessibility consultants to speed up audit-and-remediation cycles.

## How it works

1. Detection is deterministic: axe-core runs against the rendered DOM via Playwright; the model never decides whether a violation exists.
2. Remediation is grounded: a WCAG 2.2 + ARIA APG corpus embedded locally (pgvector HNSW + criterion-id boost) is retrieved per violation.
3. Every fix is verified by axe, not by the model: the Pydantic AI agent's single tool (`validate`) applies the patch to the live page and re-runs axe scoped to the parent region. The worker overrides the agent's `verified` claim with the actual validate result.
4. An eval harness gates deploys: golden WCAG fixtures, primary metric is re-run-axe pass rate; regressions block the deploy.
5. Free by design: local embeddings, free-tier model gateway (Gemini / Groq / GitHub Models / Ollama), per-request BYOK keys that never touch disk.
6. Curb audits its own home page in CI and fails the deploy on any WCAG A/AA violation.

## Stack

Python 3.12, FastAPI, Pydantic AI, Playwright + axe-core, Postgres 17 + pgvector, Redis (jobs + SSE), SvelteKit 2 / Svelte 5 frontend.
